supports.section: Understand the causes of layout shifts
supports.excerpt:
Web fonts
Downloading and rendering web fonts is typically handled in one of two ways before the web font is downloaded:

- The fallback font is swapped with the web font, incurring a Flash of Unstyled Text (FOUT).

- "Invisible" text is displayed using the fallback font until a web font is available and the text is made visible (FOIT—flash of invisible text).

skill_drafts.name: Web Font Rendering Strategy Selection
skill_drafts.description: Select between FOUT (Flash of Unstyled Text) and FOIT (Flash of Invisible Text) rendering strategies when web fonts are loading, based on user experience priorities and content visibility requirements.
skill_drafts.objective: Choose appropriate web font rendering fallback strategy to minimize layout shift and optimize user experience during font loading
applicable_signals: Fallback font available and ready to render
User interaction or page load phase where text rendering strategy matters
contraindications: Web fonts are already cached or pre-loaded
System fonts only are being used
Font loading is not a performance concern
intervention_moves: If users need immediate access to content: recommend FOUT (fallback font swaps with web font)
If layout stability is paramount: recommend FOIT (text invisible until web font ready)
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Assess content visibility priority', 'detail': 'Determine whether immediate text visibility (FOUT) or text invisibility until styled (FOIT) better serves your users'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Evaluate layout shift tolerance', 'detail': 'Consider how much layout shift is acceptable when the web font swaps in and potentially changes text dimensions'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Select rendering strategy', 'detail': 'Choose FOUT if content readability is critical; choose FOIT if layout stability is critical'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Apply and document strategy', 'detail': 'Implement the selected strategy in font-loading CSS or JavaScript and document the choice for future maintenance'}
triggers: Web fonts are being downloaded and a fallback rendering strategy must be selected
Font loading timing is a performance or user experience concern
Layout shift during font swap needs to be minimized
constraints: Strategy must be selected before web font download completes
Fallback font must be available for either strategy to work
Choice affects both visual stability and perceived performance
cautions: FOUT may cause visible text reflow when web font arrives
FOIT may delay content visibility and harm perceived performance
Strategy choice directly impacts Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) metrics
output_contract: Selected rendering strategy (FOUT or FOIT) is applied and documented; layout shift impact during font swap is minimized and measurable

metadata.prompt: When a web font is downloading, the browser must decide how to render text before the font arrives. Evaluate whether users should see unstyled text immediately (FOUT) or invisible text until the font is ready (FOIT). Choose the strategy that best balances content visibility, layout stability, and user experience for your use case.
